title: Question Tags
subtitle: Add a short question at the end of a sentence to check or confirm something.
objectives: Form a negative tag after a positive statement
Form a positive tag after a negative statement
Handle the special cases: "I am" and "Let's"

content.intro: Question tags are the short "...isn't it?" / "...don't you?" you add to the end of a sentence — very common in spoken English, to check information or invite agreement.

rules.heading: The basic rule
rules.body:
• Positive statement → negative tag: You like it, don't you?
  • Negative statement → positive tag: You don't like it, do you?
  • The tag repeats the same auxiliary/modal verb as the main sentence (is → isn't, can → can't, will → won't).

rules.heading: Special cases
rules.body:
• I am → aren't I? (not "amn't I")
  • Let's... → shall we?

examples: You're coming to the party, aren't you?
They won't be late, will they?
We can start the meeting now, can't we?
It's a beautiful day, isn't it?

commonMistakes.why: A positive statement needs a negative tag.

commonMistakes.wrong: You don't like it, don't you?
commonMistakes.right: You don't like it, do you?
commonMistakes.why: A negative statement needs a positive tag.
"Amn't" isn't standard English — the special tag for "I am" is "aren't I?"
The pronoun in the tag must match the subject of the sentence (she → she, not he).
